summary: AI observability tools have become essential as LLM-powered applications move into production, giving teams visibility into prompts, traces, latency, output quality, hallucinations, and spend. Without observability, teams cannot debug non-deterministic behavior, evaluate quality regressions, or control the rapidly compounding costs of LLM API usage. In 2026, adoption is accelerating (New Relic alone reports 30% quarter-over-quarter growth in AI monitoring), reflecting how critical these platforms are for reliability and cost governance.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: Prompts, traces, spans, token usage, latency, cost, and evaluation metrics — especially deep for LangChain/LangGraph-based applications.
features: Detailed tracing and monitoring charts with LLM-specific stats
Prompt playground and versioning
Dataset-driven evaluations and testing
Human feedback and annotation workflows
Tight native integration with the LangChain ecosystem
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39 per seat/month; overage around $2.50 per 1,000 traces at standard retention. At 100,000 traces, LangSmith Plus runs roughly $264. Trace overages can add up to 5–10% of underlying LLM API spend for trace-heavy workloads.
tools.best_for: Teams already building on LangChain/LangGraph that want deep, native tracing and evaluation in one managed platform.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: Requests, cost, token usage, and latency across 300+ models via a proxy/gateway layer.
features: One-line base-URL change integration (lightweight proxy)
Cost computation across 300+ models via model-cost repository
Per-user and per-department spend visibility
Caching and rate limiting for cost control
Fast cost governance setup (under five minutes)
tools.pricing: Free tier at 10,000 requests/month; Helicone Pro reaches the 100,000-trace milestone at around $79 — a lower price point than many trace-metered competitors.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting instant, low-overhead cost visibility and governance across multiple model providers without framework lock-in.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B / Weave)
tools.monitors: LLM traces, experiments, model evaluations, prompt performance, and ML/LLM lifecycle metrics.
features: W&B Weave for LLM application tracing and evaluation
Experiment tracking and model versioning
Evaluation dashboards and comparison tooling
Integration with the broader ML experimentation ecosystem
Collaboration and reporting features for teams
tools.pricing: Free personal tier; team/enterprise pricing is consumption- and seat-based (custom enterprise quotes for larger deployments).
tools.best_for: ML and AI teams that want unified experiment tracking plus LLM observability across the model development lifecycle.

tools.name: Arize AI (Phoenix)
tools.monitors: Production LLM/ML performance, evaluations, embeddings, RAG quality, drift, and hallucination detection.
features: Open-source Phoenix for evaluation and tracing
OpenTelemetry-based integration
RAG and retrieval quality analysis
Drift and performance-degradation detection
Embedding visualization and troubleshooting
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is open-source and free to self-host; Arize AX (enterprise/cloud) uses custom, consumption-based enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams needing open, standards-based (OpenTelemetry) evaluation and production monitoring, especially for RAG and drift detection.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: Traces, spans, token usage, cost, latency, evaluations, and prompt management — with strong self-hosting support.
features: Open-source trace store that can be self-hosted
Evaluation and quality scoring built on top of traces
Alerting and monitoring dashboards
Prompt management and versioning
Cost-control friendly for high-volume workloads
tools.pricing: Open-source and free to self-host; managed cloud offers a free tier with paid usage-based plans. Self-hosting is a popular cost-control alternative to per-trace billing.
tools.best_for: Self-hosted teams wanting an open-source, cost-efficient observability stack with evals and alerting built in.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM traces, spans, token usage, and latency using open standards exportable to many backends.
features: Built on OpenTelemetry standards for broad compatibility
Vendor-neutral instrumentation of LLM calls
Exports telemetry to existing observability backends (Datadog, Grafana, etc.)
Open-source SDKs for Python and JavaScript/Node.js
Avoids vendor lock-in by using standard formats
tools.pricing: Open-source and free; costs are only those of the backend you export telemetry to (e.g., your existing APM provider).
tools.best_for: Teams that want standards-based, vendor-neutral LLM instrumentation that plugs into existing observability infrastructure.

cost_tips: Use a gateway/proxy (like Helicone) with response caching to avoid paying for repeated or identical LLM calls, and set per-user or per-department rate limits for cost governance.
Match the model to the task — route simple queries to smaller, cheaper models and reserve large frontier models for complex reasoning, which can dramatically cut token spend.

Watch observability overhead itself: per-trace billing can add 5–10% on top of LLM API spend for trace-heavy workloads, so consider self-hosting (Langfuse, Arize Phoenix) or sampling traces at high volume.
Optimize prompts and context — trim system prompts, compress or summarize long context, and cap max output tokens to reduce per-request token consumption.
